A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COGNOS research work. All 22 pages of v2 and 26 pages of v3, including Appendices A–D, support comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures despite pagination changes.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices C–D report original benchmark results, component ablations, residual diagnostics, sensitivity analyses and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V3 retains these empirical results and additionally reports an original standalone Anomaly Transformer evaluation in Appendix D.5.

M1.justification: The stated computations receive limited corrections: Eq. (5) removes an extra log K offset from the spectral loss, and Eq. (16) uses the inflated prior covariance, consistent with Appendix A.3. The GWNR–ARKS components and Algorithm 1 remain; the PDFs do not establish an implementation redesign.

E1.justification: Both evaluate GECCO, MSL, SMAP, PSM, SWAN, SWaT and UCR with the same dataset coverage. The new Anomaly Transformer comparison uses five retained datasets. SMAP and SWAN ablations omitted from v3's shortened Table 3 remain in Table 9.

E2.justification: Anomaly Transformer, previously discussed only as related work, is newly evaluated as a standalone comparator on five datasets in Appendix D.5 and Table 11. The nine original backbone comparisons and moving-average/low-pass filter comparators remain.

E3.justification: The added Anomaly Transformer evaluation separately reports Precision and Recall alongside F1 and affiliation measures in Table 11. Existing splits, training budgets and backbone configurations are retained. The quantile-threshold pipeline, calibration source, buffer setting and UCR averaging are newly documented settings, not demonstrated changes to existing protocols.

E4.justification: The existing component ablation receives revised evidence: Table 9 changes GECCO vanilla Std-F1 from 0.4261 to 0.4738 and ARKS-only from 0.4738 to 0.4740, substantially reducing its apparent standalone contribution. Ablation configurations, confidence-level sensitivity tests and qualitative case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both specify random seed 2025 and retain the same 95% white-noise confidence bands for autocorrelation diagnostics. V3 adds no repeated-run counts, across-run uncertainty estimates or statistical comparison procedures.

E6.justification: Table 7 revises KANAD–GECCO vanilla R-A-R from 0.7204 to 0.9761 and R-A-P from 0.0789 to 0.5810, reversing comparisons with unchanged COGNOS scores of 0.9753 and 0.5040. Table 8 changes TimeMixer++–COGNOS SMAP Std-F1 from 0.0808 to 0.2206. Several baseline/ablation F1 entries are harmonized, and Table 11 adds Anomaly Transformer results; most existing results remain.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 substantially revises the central optimality argument. V2 claims GWNR makes both noise sources Gaussian and derives Kalman–MMSE equivalence. V3 replaces that derivation with measurement-noise regularization plus an explicit Gaussian process-noise assumption, and adds diagonal-covariance/spatial-independence conditions for extending channel-wise optimality to multivariate data.

C1.justification: The principal GWNR–ARKS contributions and cross-backbone enhancement claims remain. V3's conclusion adds an explicit claim that residual engineering requires no modification to the inference protocol and identifies extensions beyond MSE objectives as future work, making the applicability boundary more explicit.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive COGNOS-specific limitations concerning fixed observation-noise variance, non-MSE objectives and anomaly-duration coverage. Unlike v2's largely favorable onset-detection discussion, it explicitly acknowledges range-metric decreases and their practical disadvantage. It also expands explanations of component failures, buffer latency versus stability, and the offline-versus-streaming timing comparison.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-repository pointer, internal constants and RBF bandwidths in Table 6, the experimental buffer setting k = w − 1, training-set calibration, and averaging over 250 UCR subsets. Appendix D.2 documents the 98%–99.5% quantile search and event construction; D.3 supplies moving-average window 20 and Butterworth cutoff 0.05. These substantially improve reproducibility documentation without establishing changed prior settings.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged. Section 2.3 removes the claim that end-to-end Kalman hybrids can produce degenerate solutions, retaining the decoupling distinction. V3 also explicitly positions Anomaly Transformer outside COGNOS's enhancement scope while evaluating it independently.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized wording and grammar corrections, replaces placeholder affiliations, expands result explanations and the conclusion, and introduces labeled limitations and additional appendix subsections. The overall narrative, main section order and most existing prose remain.

P2.justification: Table 3 becomes a three-dataset, single-column display while full ablations remain in Table 9. Table 6 gains an internal-parameter block, Table 11 is added, and Algorithm 1 moves to a separate page. Existing figures are retained with limited caption/reflow changes; appendix pagination introduces substantial blank space, especially page 24.

improvement.justification: V3 improves auditability through implementation and thresholding disclosures, corrects several inconsistent result entries, and better qualifies the noise assumptions and applicability limits. The standalone baseline adds useful context. The improvement remains limited: threshold-selection details are incomplete, broad optimality language persists, and Table 2 retains the GECCO vanilla average 0.5475 although its revised entries average approximately 0.5531.
